export const SAMPLE_DOC = `# Launch plan for the new onboarding flow

This document is a very rough draft. Select any paragraph, pick an action in the bar above, and the co-author will propose changes as tracked edits you can accept or reject one by one.

## Why we are doing this

Right now a lot of new users basically drop off before they actually create their first project. We think that the main reason is that the setup screen asks for too many things in order to get started, and it's really not clear what happens next.

## What we will ship

- A shorter setup form with only the fields we truly need
- A sample project that is created automatically
- A checklist that shows the three steps to a first result

## Risks

The checklist could feel patronising to experienced users. We should utilize a dismiss button and remember the choice. We also just don't know yet whether the sample project should be deleted after the first real one is created.

## Open questions

1. Do we show the checklist on mobile?
2. Who writes the copy for the empty states?
`;

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
entries.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
entries.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
entries.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
entries.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

content.text:
Picked up where the grok session was cut off, verified its work, and closed the one gap that caused the "it's not translating" report.

**Answer to the open question: yes, it was mocked.** There is no `.env.local` in the repo, only `.env.example`. Without a key the suggest route returns `missing_key`, so the dev server grok ran used `MOCK_AI=1`. The old mock only stripped filler words, so a translate request came back as English with a few words removed. Grok added canned Portuguese, Spanish and Chinese versions of the sample document to the mock before the session ended. Real translation of arbitrary text needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in `.env.local`.

**What I changed** in `src/lib/mock.ts`: the mock matched the document byte for byte against the sample, so a sample you had already edited with "Improve" or "Shorten" still got no translation. It now matches on the first heading, so an edited sample is translated too. Any other document gets a `(zh-CN)` style marker, which is the mock's deliberate ceiling.

**Verified:**
- Type check, lint and `next build` all pass with grok's changes plus mine.
- In mock mode the API returns the full Portuguese and Chinese documents for both the pristine and an edited sample.
- Headless Chrome renders the page with the interface language selector, the "Text language" selector with flags, and the sample document.

**Not verified:** the click-through in a real browser. The Chrome extension could not inject scripts into localhost pages here, on both the dev and production servers, so I could not drive the selector or screenshot the tracked edits. A production build in mock mode is still running at http://localhost:3124 if you want to click through it yourself. Stop it with:

```
kill $(lsof -t -iTCP:3124 -sTCP:LISTEN)
```

**Two things left for you:**
- The grok transcript snapshot in `.grok/sessions/` is a partial copy. The complete one now exists, but copying it from your home directory was blocked by the permission classifier. If you want it refreshed:

```
cp ~/.grok/sessions/%2FUsers%2Ffilipe%2FDeveloper%2Fchiri-challenge/01a1895f-b297-7151-bbb1-a481cdb657d0/chat_history.jsonl .grok/sessions/01a1895f-b297-7151-bbb1-a481cdb657d0/chat_history.jsonl

- Nothing is committed yet. The whole language feature, the mock fix and the session logs are sitting in the working tree, ready for a commit when you want one.

# Example: Browser-driven web app

You have a dev server that serves HTML to a browser. An agent in a
headless container can't open a browser window - so "run the app" means
launching the dev server, driving a headless Chromium against it, and
producing a screenshot that proves the page rendered.

Don't write a browser driver. Use `chromium-cli`.

## Dev server

Find the dev command (`package.json` `scripts.dev`, `Makefile`,
README), start it in the background, and wait for it to actually serve:

```bash
npm run dev &   # or yarn dev, pnpm dev, make serve, ./dev.sh
timeout 30 bash -c 'until curl -sf http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
```

Don't `sleep 5` - poll the port. Stop by killing the port's listener
-- `lsof -ti:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs -r kill` - before relaunching,
or the next run hits `EADDRINUSE`. (`$!` after `npm run dev &` is only
the npm wrapper; npm doesn't forward SIGTERM to the server it spawned,
so the port kill is what actually frees it.) Avoid `pkill -f` with a
broad pattern - it can match the agent's own command line and kill the
session.

## Drive

`chromium-cli` is a headless-Chromium REPL. Pipe a script to stdin:

```bash
chromium-cli --session app <<'EOF'
nav http://localhost:3000
wait-for text=Dashboard
screenshot
click button:has-text("New item")
fill input[name="title"] Smoke test
press Enter
wait-for text=Smoke test
screenshot
console --errors
EOF
```

Screenshots land in `chromium_cli/sessions/app/screenshots/` (latest
symlinked as `screenshot.png`). That's the whole loop: `nav` ->
`wait-for` the element you need -> act (`click` / `fill` / `type` /
`press`) -> `screenshot` -> `console --errors` to check nothing threw.
Full command reference: `chromium-cli` skill, or `help` at the prompt.

For iterative debugging, run it under tmux and `send-keys` one command
at a time - same commands, same session.

**If `chromium-cli` isn't available:** adapt
[electron.md](electron.md)'s REPL driver - the structure and commands
transfer, but it's `_electron`-specific:
import `{ chromium }` instead, launch with
`chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox'] })`, acquire the page via
`(await app.newContext()).newPage()` then `goto()` your dev URL, and
drop the Electron-only window introspection
(`.windows()`/`.firstWindow()`/the `windows` command).

## What to put in the skill

The project-specific bits only. `chromium-cli` handles the mechanics.

- **Dev command + port + stop.** The exact start line, any env vars it
  needs, and the `kill` to stop it.
- **Auth.** Whatever gets a logged-in session - a `set-cookie` line, a
  `fill`/`click` login sequence, or a helper script that does the API
  dance and emits the cookie.
- **One representative interaction.** Not the whole app - one path that
  proves it's running, ending in a screenshot.
- **App-specific gotchas.** Only the ones you actually hit.

## Gotchas that recur

- **React controlled inputs.** `eval el.value = '...'` doesn't fire
  React's onChange. Use `fill` / `type` - they go through Playwright's
  input pipeline.
- **Websockets / long-poll.** `wait-idle` never settles. `wait-for` the
  element you actually need.
- **Slow first paint.** Vite/Next compile routes on demand; the first
  `nav` can take 10s+. `wait-for` handles it; raw `sleep` doesn't.
- **`screenshot-element <sel>`** crops to one element - use it when the
  diff is in a specific component, not the whole page.
- **Check `console --errors` before declaring success.** A page can
  render its shell while every data fetch 500s.

- **Auth.** Whatever gets a logged-in session - a `set-cookie` line, a
  `fill`/`click` login sequence, or a helper script that does the API
  dance and emits the cookie.
- **One representative interaction.** Not the whole app - one path that
  proves it's running, ending in a screenshot.
- **App-specific gotchas.** Only the ones you actually hit.

## Gotchas that recur

- **React controlled inputs.** `eval el.value = '...'` doesn't fire
  React's onChange. Use `fill` / `type` - they go through Playwright's
  input pipeline.
- **Websockets / long-poll.** `wait-idle` never settles. `wait-for` the
  element you actually need.
- **Slow first paint.** Vite/Next compile routes on demand; the first
  `nav` can take 10s+. `wait-for` handles it; raw `sleep` doesn't.
- **`screenshot-element <sel>`** crops to one element - use it when the
  diff is in a specific component, not the whole page.
- **Check `console --errors` before declaring success.** A page can
  render its shell while every data fetch 500s.

# Deploy to Vercel

Deploy the current project to Vercel using the CLI, with preflight safety checks, explicit production confirmation, and post-deploy verification.

## Preflight

Run these checks before any deployment. Stop on failure and print actionable guidance.

1. **CLI available?** — Confirm `vercel` is on PATH.
   - If missing: `npm i -g vercel` (or `pnpm add -g vercel` / `bun add -g vercel`).
2. **Project linked?** — Check for `.vercel/project.json` in the current directory or nearest parent.
   - If not found: run `vercel link` interactively, then re-run `/deploy`.
3. **Monorepo detection** — Look for `turbo.json` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` at the repo root.
   - If detected: confirm which package is targeted. If ambiguous, ask the user before proceeding.
4. **Uncommitted changes** — Run `git status --porcelain`.
   - If output is non-empty: warn the user that uncommitted changes will **not** be included in the deploy. Ask whether to continue or commit first.
   - If not a git repo, skip this check.
5. **Observability preflight** (production deploys only) —

Before promoting to production, verify observability readiness:

- **Drains check**: Query configured drains via MCP `list_drains` or REST API. If no drains are configured on a Pro/Enterprise plan, warn:
  > ⚠️ No drains configured. Production errors won't be forwarded to external monitoring.
  > Configure drains via Dashboard or REST API before promoting.
- **Errored drains**: If any drain is in error state, warn and suggest remediation before deploying:
  > ⚠️ Drain "<url>" is errored. Fix or recreate before production deploy to avoid monitoring gaps.
- **Error monitoring**: Check that at least one of these is in place: configured drains, an error tracking integration (e.g., Sentry, Datadog via `vercel integration ls`), or `@vercel/analytics` in the project.
- These are warnings, not blockers — the user may proceed after acknowledgment.

## Plan

State the intended action before executing:

- **Preview deploy** (default): `vercel` — creates a preview deployment on a unique URL.
- **Production deploy**: `vercel --prod` — deploys to production domains.

If "" contains "prod" or "production":

### Preview Deployment

<!-- Sourced from deployments-cicd skill: Deployment Commands > Preview Deployment -->
```bash

### Production Deployment (requires confirmation)

<!-- Sourced from deployments-cicd skill: Deployment Commands > Production Deployment -->
```bash
# Deploy directly to production
vercel --prod

After deployment completes, verify the result:

### 1. Inspect the Deployment

<!-- Sourced from deployments-cicd skill: Deployment Commands > Inspect Deployments -->
```bash

# List recent deployments

Extract: deployment state (READY / ERROR / QUEUED / BUILDING), build duration, framework, Node.js version, function count.

| Finding | Action |
|---------|--------|
| No errors | ✓ Clean deploy — no runtime errors in first hour |

findings.failure_scenario:
MOCK_AI=1, document "Hello world" (no heading, no trailing newline), pick pt-BR → mock returns "Hello world

(pt-BR)
". Accepting adds a trailing newline the user never typed; with a selection target, the extra newline splits the following paragraph.

findings.short_summary: CANON en-US duplicates SAMPLE_DOC; H1 match depends on them matching
findings.summary: CANON["en-US"] is a verbatim copy of SAMPLE_DOC from src/lib/sample.ts; mockTranslation's H1 match depends on the two staying identical, so the duplicate is a drift hazard.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone rewords the sample's title in sample.ts → the H1 match no longer recognizes the default document → mock translation of the demo doc degrades to the "(pt-BR)" marker with no error. Use `"en-US": SAMPLE_DOC` directly.

findings.short_summary: Mock detects translation by regex on human-readable prompt text
findings.summary: Mock translation is detected by regex-matching the instruction produced by translateInstruction(); the two live in different files with no shared constant, so a wording tweak silently downgrades mock translation to the generic prose rewrite.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone edits translateInstruction to start with "Translate this text into …" → TRANSLATE no longer matches → mockRewrite applies the filler-word rewrite instead, while the UI still treats it as a translation and flips docLocale on accept. Send translateTo in the request body or share one prefix constant.

findings.short_summary: CJK font rule keyed to UI locale and body only
findings.summary: The CJK font rule is keyed to the UI locale (html[lang] is set from `locale`), not the document language, and it only touches `body`, so Chinese document text in the Preview under an English UI, and in the editor or chunk buttons under any UI, never gets it.
findings.failure_scenario: UI en-US, document translated to zh-CN: Preview renders Chinese via system fallback; the editor uses the mono font variable and the chunk buttons the sans variable, which this rule does not reach. Append the CJK fallbacks to the base body font stack and delete the [lang] rule.

findings.short_summary: clearTranslation runs twice on every HTTP error
findings.summary: clearTranslation() is called on the HTTP-error path right before `throw new Error("request")`, and the catch block calls it again for the same condition.
findings.failure_scenario: Dead duplicate: every !res.ok response runs clearTranslation twice. Delete the first call; the catch already covers it.

findings.short_summary: readDocLocale duplicates readLocale and hardcodes en-US
findings.summary: readDocLocale duplicates readLocale's try/catch localStorage read and hardcodes "en-US" instead of the exported DEFAULT_LOCALE.
findings.failure_scenario: Changing DEFAULT_LOCALE in i18n.ts leaves the document default on en-US. A single readStoredLocale(key, fallback) in i18n.ts serves both callers.

findings.short_summary: translateTo state and translateBase ref form a two-field invariant
findings.summary: translateTo (state) and translateBase (ref) are always written and cleared together, creating a two-field invariant maintained by clearTranslation() and three call sites.
findings.failure_scenario: Any future path that sets one without the other leaves a stale base or a dangling locale. One useState<{ to: Locale; base: string } | null> removes clearTranslation() and the invariant.

findings.short_summary: Custom mergeControls re-implements the library's buttons
findings.summary: The custom mergeControls builder re-implements the library's own button rendering just to swap the label; CodeMirror's i18n hook for this is EditorState.phrases, which the built-in path already consults via state.phrase("Accept"/"Reject").
findings.failure_scenario: Nine lines duplicate @codemirror/merge's default, and any upstream change to the default buttons (aria attributes, classes) is not inherited. EditorState.phrases.of({ Accept, Reject }) in a Compartment keeps mergeControls: true. The querySelectorAll relabel effect is still needed for live switches either way.

findings.short_summary: Reject all after partial inline accepts leaves docLocale stale
findings.summary: finish("rejectAll") never calls keepTranslationIfDocChanged, so a translation that was partially accepted inline leaves the document in the new language while docLocale and the select still claim the old one; the inline onChunks(0) path flips it, so the two review paths disagree.
findings.failure_scenario: Translate en-US → pt-BR, accept 3 of 5 chunks inline, click "Reject all" (or re-select English in the text-language select, which routes to finish("rejectAll")). Editor.rejectAll restores the merge view's original doc, which already contains the 3 accepted chunks, so the doc is mostly Portuguese but docLocale stays en-US and is persisted that way. Fix: call keepTranslationIfDocChanged() in finish() for both actions.

findings.short_summary: Mock H1 match swaps a selection for the whole canned document
findings.summary: The H1 match keys on the target's first line, so a selection that starts with the sample heading is replaced by the entire canonical document, duplicating the rest of the doc.
findings.failure_scenario: MOCK_AI=1, select only the title line and send the translate instruction (via the bar or /api/suggest) → mock returns the full pt-BR document in place of one line → document now contains the whole doc twice. Gate the canon swap on the target being the whole document (the route already knows `whole`).

findings.short_summary: Long documents can never be translated; error advice is unusable
findings.summary: Translation forces target = null (whole document), so any document over MAX_WHOLE_DOC_CHARS can never be translated, and the error copy it gets ("Select a section instead") is advice the language select cannot act on.
findings.failure_scenario: Paste a 25,000-char document, pick 中文 in "Text language" → server returns document_too_long → UI says to select a section. User selects a paragraph and picks the language again → identical error, because run() discards the selection when options.translateTo is set. Either honor the selection for translation (translate only the range, docLocale unchanged) or show a translation-specific message.

findings.short_summary: Picking a language during review discards the open proposal
findings.summary: Choosing a document language while reviewing a non-translation proposal silently rejectAll()s that proposal; if the translation request then fails, the catch path sets review to null and the previous proposal is gone with only a generic error.
findings.failure_scenario: Ask "Improve" on the whole doc, get 8 suggested changes, then pick Español in the text-language select while the network is down. run() calls ed.rejectAll(), fetch throws, catch sees refining=false → setMode("idle"), setReview(null). findings.short_summary: Manual edit during review flips docLocale after full reject

A revisão terminou e os 15 achados estão no painel acima, ordenados por gravidade. Minha triagem, como engenheiro cético:

**Corrigir antes do próximo deploy** (bugs reais, diffs pequenos):
- "Rejeitar tudo" depois de aceitar alguns trechos de uma tradução deixa o documento meio traduzido, mas o idioma do texto fica no antigo e é persistido assim.
- No mock, uma seleção que começa pelo título vira o documento canônico inteiro, duplicando o texto. Bug meu de hoje, no match pelo H1.
- O mock pula o `cleanReply` da rota real e duplica a lógica de espaço em branco com uma versão mais fraca. Apagar o helper e passar pela rota resolve dois achados de uma vez.
- `CANON["en-US"]` é cópia literal do `SAMPLE_DOC`. Uma referência direta elimina o risco de desalinhar.
- `clearTranslation` roda duas vezes em todo erro HTTP. Apagar uma linha.

**Decisões de produto, não corrijo sem você dizer:**
- Tradução sempre pega o documento inteiro, então documentos acima de 20 mil caracteres nunca traduzem e a mensagem de erro manda selecionar um trecho, o que o seletor não consegue fazer. Ou honrar a seleção, ou mensagem específica.
- Trocar o idioma do texto durante uma revisão de "Melhorar" descarta a proposta em silêncio, e se a tradução falhar ela se perde.

**Deixaria como está** (refatorações sem bug): o par `translateTo`/`translateBase`, o `readDocLocale` duplicado, e o `mergeControls` custom em vez de `EditorState.phrases`. Mudam forma, não comportamento.

**Nota crítica geral:** a i18n de erros parou no meio. Três erros viraram códigos, mas os seis de validação e o 502 do upstream chegam como prosa em inglês e aparecem crus numa interface em chinês. Ou codifica tudo, ou volta a prosa.

Se quiser, aplico o primeiro bloco agora, rodo o typecheck, lint e o teste da tradução de novo, e fico pronto para o `vercel --prod` assim que a chave estiver na Vercel.

# Brief: fix one review finding in an isolated copy

The app is a Next.js 16 Markdown editor with an AI co-author (CodeMirror merge view, OpenRouter API route, `MOCK_AI=1` mock mode, four locales: pt-BR, en-US, es-AR, zh-CN). A code review produced the 15 findings below. Fifteen agents work in parallel, **one finding each**.

## Rules

- `W` = `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-filipe-Developer-chiri-challenge/9bff265c-535d-461e-8dbf-8e24930d3447/scratchpad/wt`
- Your working copy is `$W/fNN` (NN = your finding number, two digits). Edit **only** files inside your copy. Never touch `$W/base`, other copies, or `/Users/filipe/Developer/chiri-challenge`.
- Fix **only your finding**. Other agents fix the others at the same time, and the main agent merges all patches afterwards, so touching unrelated code causes merge conflicts. Keep the diff as small as a careful senior engineer would. No drive-by refactors, no new dependencies, no new files unless unavoidable.
- Read the code your finding touches end to end before editing. Line numbers below refer to the copy as you receive it.
- Any new user-facing string must be added to all four locales in `src/lib/i18n.ts` (the `Messages` type plus each locale object). Match the tone of the existing copy.
- Verify in your copy: `cd $W/fNN && npx tsc --noEmit -p . && npm run lint`. Both must pass. If your change has non-trivial logic, also run a quick check (for example a `node`/`npx tsx` one-off against the function) and say what you ran. Do not start dev servers on ports 3000 or 3123/3124; if you need one, use port `40NN`, and kill it before you finish.
- Write your patch: `cd $W && diff -ruN base/src fNN/src > fNN.patch` (exit code 1 from diff is normal). Make sure the patch contains only your change.
- Final reply, at most ~10 lines: what you changed and why, files touched, verification commands and results, and any risk of conflict with another finding you noticed.

## Findings (owner = number)

1. `src/components/App.tsx:210` — `finish("rejectAll")` never calls `keepTranslationIfDocChanged`, so after accepting some translation chunks inline then clicking Reject all, the doc is partly translated but `docLocale` stays old. Fix: make both review exits agree (call it in `finish` for both actions).
2. `src/lib/mock.ts:108` — mock canon swap keys on the target's first line, so a *selection* starting with the sample H1 is replaced by the whole canned document (duplicates the doc). Fix: only swap when the target is the whole document (the route knows `whole` from `splitDocument`; pass it into `mockRewrite` or equivalent).
3. `src/components/App.tsx:152` — translation always targets the whole doc, so docs over `MAX_WHOLE_DOC_CHARS` can never be translated and the error says "Select a section instead", which the language select cannot act on. **Decided default:** keep whole-document translation; when a *translation* fails with `document_too_long`, show a translation-specific message in all four locales (e.g. "The document is too long to translate in one go."). content.text:
Os 15 achados foram corrigidos e aplicados ao repositório. Typecheck, lint e build passam, e o app roda sem erros de console no Chrome headless.

**Como rodou:** cada um dos 15 subagentes corrigiu um achado numa cópia isolada do código e devolveu um patch. Dez patches entraram limpos. O achado 2 conflitou com o 7 em `mock.ts`. Os achados 4, 5 e 14 colidiram em `run()` e `finish()`. Esses quatro eu juntei à mão.

**Uma decisão de fusão para você saber:** o achado 5 passou a decidir o idioma do texto pelo que foi aceito da proposta. O editor agora rastreia o texto proposto em vez de comparar com uma cópia do documento. Com isso a cópia sumiu, e o achado 14 virou só remover o `clearTranslation` e deixar um único estado. É a maior mudança do lote, com cerca de 30 linhas novas no editor.

**Defaults que escolhi para as duas decisões de produto:**
- **Documento longo:** a tradução continua no documento inteiro. Quando ele passa do limite, aparece uma mensagem própria de tradução nos quatro idiomas.
- **Proposta descartada:** se a tradução falha durante a revisão de um "Melhorar", a proposta anterior volta e a revisão continua.

**O que verifiquei no app rodando, em modo mock:**
- Traduzir, aceitar, recarregar, trocar a interface para chinês, "Melhorar" e "Rejeitar tudo" funcionam como antes.
- Selecionar só o título e traduzir agora marca a linha com `(pt-BR)`. Antes o documento era duplicado.
- Um modelo inválido devolve um código de erro em vez de texto cru em inglês. Um documento longo devolve o erro próprio.
- Aceitar o trecho da tradução troca o idioma do texto. Editar à mão durante a revisão e depois rejeitar tudo não troca.

**Ainda não verificado:** o mock gera um único trecho por tradução, então não deu para testar no navegador o caso de aceitar só alguns trechos e depois rejeitar tudo. O agente do achado 5 cobriu esse caso com seis cenários contra o estado real do CodeMirror, e todos passaram.

**O site na Vercel ainda está na versão antiga e sem chave.** Para publicar estas correções, adicione a chave com o comando abaixo e me avise. Aí eu rodo `vercel --prod` e confiro o site.

```
grep '^OPENROUTER_API_KEY=' .env.local | cut -d= -f2- | vercel env add OPENROUTER_API_KEY production
```

O servidor local com a chave real continua em http://localhost:3000, já com as correções. Nada foi commitado.

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

content.text:
Na prática, nenhuma das três opções custa dinheiro neste projeto. O que muda entre elas é com que frequência o cache acerta e quanta complexidade entra no código.

**Quanto custa a tradução que o cache evita**, estimado a partir dos preços configurados no app:

| Documento | Haiku 5.5 | Sonnet 5.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Documento de exemplo, cerca de 1.300 caracteres | US$ 0,0003 | US$ 0,005 |
| Documento no limite, 20 mil caracteres | US$ 0,003 | US$ 0,06 |

A chave tem US$ 5 de limite. Mesmo sem cache, são milhares de traduções do exemplo com Haiku. O cache economiza de verdade quando muitos revisores usam o Sonnet.

**Custo de cada opção:**
- **Memória da instância.** Custa zero e não adiciona dependências. Ocupa no máximo uns 12 MB de RAM com um teto de 200 traduções. Por outro lado, perde tudo a cada deploy ou quando a Vercel sobe uma instância nova, e instâncias diferentes não compartilham o cache. Num demo com pouco tráfego, normalmente uma instância atende todo mundo, então acerta bem.
- **Vercel Runtime Cache.** É grátis no plano Hobby até 1 milhão de leituras e 200 mil escritas por mês, e cada tradução gasta de 1 a 8 unidades. Se passar disso, não há cobrança: o cache só pausa até o fim do ciclo. Ele sobrevive a deploys e é compartilhado entre instâncias da mesma região. O custo real é de código: entra o pacote `@vercel/functions`, cada consulta faz uma chamada de rede de poucos milissegundos, e no Hobby o espaço é dividido com seus outros projetos. Eu ainda precisaria confirmar como ele se comporta fora da Vercel, no `npm run dev`.
- **No navegador.** Custa zero no servidor e tem o código mais simples para o caso de ida e volta. Mas cada pessoa tem o próprio cache, então dez revisores traduzindo o exemplo pagam dez vezes.

**Minha recomendação é memória da instância.** O dinheiro em jogo é de centavos, e ela entrega a ida e volta e a repetição sem nenhuma dependência. Se o demo ganhar tráfego ou muitos revisores usarem o Sonnet, a troca para o Runtime Cache fica restrita a uma função.

Me diga qual opção prefere que eu monto o plano e implemento.

content.text:
A causa está no prompt. Com um documento longo em chinês, o Haiku 5.5 perde a instrução de tradução que vem antes do texto. Ele obedece à última linha do prompt, "retorne apenas o documento revisado", e devolve o chinês intacto. Como o texto volta idêntico, o editor não vê nenhuma diferença e mostra "O coautor não encontrou nada para mudar aqui". O bug está em produção, porque o Haiku é o modelo padrão.

Testei o documento de exemplo em chinês traduzido para pt-BR, três vezes por variante:

| Variante | Modelo | Resultado |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt atual | Haiku 5.5 | Chinês intacto, 3 de 3 |
| Prompt atual | GPT-6 Luna e Sonnet 5.5 | Traduz |
| Nome do idioma em inglês | Haiku 5.5 | Chinês intacto, 3 de 3 |
| Sem a regra de devolver o texto intacto | Haiku 5.5 | Chinês intacto, 3 de 3 |
| Instrução depois do texto | Haiku 5.5 | Traduz, 3 de 3 |
| Idioma repetido na última linha | Haiku 5.5 | Traduz, 3 de 3 |
| Inglês para pt-BR, ou chinês para inglês | Haiku 5.5 | Traduz |

Os testes custaram cerca de US$ 0,012 da chave.

**Correção que eu proponho:** em `src/lib/prompt.ts`, colocar a instrução depois do texto e do contexto, logo antes da linha final. Assim ela é a última coisa que o modelo lê. É a recomendação geral para prompts com documentos longos e vale para todas as ações, não só para tradução. É uma mudança de poucas linhas na montagem da mensagem.

**Um segundo ajuste que vale fazer junto:** quando uma tradução volta idêntica ao original, o app hoje diz que não havia nada para mudar, o que engana. Uma mensagem de falha específica de tradução deixaria claro que o modelo falhou.

O cache de traduções continua esperando a sua escolha de onde guardar. Se você aprovar a correção do prompt, eu aplico, testo de novo com o Haiku e publico.

Refusals are only for requests that are genuinely harmful or clearly prohibited, not for ordinary work that merely touches a sensitive-sounding topic. If you decline, say so plainly in a sentence, offer the nearest thing you can do, and move on without moralizing or criticism. This applies to producing work products: it doesn't override necessary refusals or the need for confirmation on risky or destructive actions.

# Writing for the user
The user may not see your tool calls, tool results, or the text you write between them. Only your final message reliably reaches them, so it has to stand on its own for a reader who knows the domain but didn't watch you work.

Rules for that message:
- Lead with the answer or outcome. If something could not be verified, say so first. Keep it short by leaving things out, not by packing them in.
- One idea per sentence, about 20 words, with a verb. Short does not mean clipped: a sentence beats a label with a colon. Start a new sentence instead of joining clauses with a semicolon.
- No em-dashes, no parentheticals, no arrows.
- State facts and conclusions. Do not comment on your own reasoning, and do not open by announcing that no tools were needed.
- Do not refer to anything by a name you made up during the session. Expand uncommon acronyms the first time you use them. Say who wrote a message and what it said, not by number or label.
- Keep code out of prose. Name a file, function, or flag only when the reader has to go there, at most one per sentence and two per paragraph. Describe the rest in words. Commands, snippets, and error text go in a fenced code block.
- Keep numbers out of prose. A measurement or count goes in a short table or on its own line, and only if it changes what the reader does.
- Use a bulleted or numbered list for parallel items: findings, steps, options, files to look at. One or two sentences per bullet, never a paragraph. Bold the first few words of a bullet or paragraph, never a whole sentence. A single point or a line of argument stays in prose.
- No headers in a message under about 500 words. Above that, at most three. If the user asks for no formatting, use none.
- Stop when the content stops. No closing offer, no restating what you did.

You are operating autonomously. The user is not watching in real time and cannot answer questions mid-task, so asking 'Want me to…?' or 'Shall I…?' will block the work. For reversible actions that follow from the original request, proceed without asking. Stop only for destructive actions or genuine scope changes the user must decide. Offering follow-ups after the task is done is fine; asking permission before doing the work is not.

Exception: when the user is describing a problem, asking a question, or thinking out loud rather than requesting a change, the deliverable is your assessment. Report your findings and stop. Don't apply a fix until they ask for one.

Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph. If it is a plan, an analysis, a question, a list of next steps, or a promise about work you have not done ('I'll…', 'let me know when…'), do that work now with tool calls. That includes retrying after errors and gathering missing information yourself. Do not stop because the context or session is long. End your turn only when the task is complete or you are blocked on input only the user can provide.

Before running a command that changes system state (such as restarts, deletes, or config edits), check that the evidence actually supports that specific action. A signal that pattern-matches to a known failure may have a different cause.

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.
