* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

description.description: New description for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

# OpenRouter key (https://openrouter.ai/keys). Never commit the real one.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=

# Set to 1 to run without a key: the API returns a fake deterministic rewrite.
# Mock "translations" are canned copies of the sample document (matched by its
# first heading), not translations of your text; other documents only get a marker.
MOCK_AI=
# Changelog

A Markdown editor with an AI co-author. Select text (or nothing, for the whole document), ask for a change, and review the result as tracked edits.

Live demo: https://chiri-challenge.vercel.app

## What is implemented

### Editor and review
- Markdown editor (CodeMirror 6) with a live rendered preview side by side.
- AI suggestions shown as tracked changes in a unified merge view. Accept or reject each change inline, or all at once.
- Works on the selection, or on the whole document when nothing is selected. A selection gets the surrounding text and the document outline as context.
- Refine a suggestion with a follow-up instruction. The co-author keeps the earlier rounds as history. A failed refine keeps the previous suggestion.
- Six quick actions (Improve, Shorten, Expand, Fix grammar, More formal, More casual) plus a free-text instruction box (⌘K).
- The document is saved in the browser. A pending suggestion is never saved.

### Languages
- Interface in English, Brazilian Portuguese, Argentine Spanish, and Simplified Chinese. Defaults to the browser language and is remembered.
- "Text language" selector, with flags, translates the whole document with the co-author as tracked changes.
- The document language changes only when translated text is kept, inline or with Accept all. Manual edits during review do not count.
- Chinese text gets CJK font fallbacks in the editor, the preview, and the buttons.

### Cost and safety
- Curated model menu: Claude Haiku 5.5 (default), GPT-6 Luna, and Claude Sonnet 5.5. The API rejects any other model, so the demo key cannot be pointed at an expensive one.
- Cost of the last request and of the session in the footer, plus the remaining demo budget.
- Requests stop when the shared key has less than $0.50 left.
- Whole-document edits are capped at 20,000 characters.
- Translation cache: repeating a translation is free, and translating back restores the original text without calling the model.
- Server errors are codes, shown in the interface language. Upstream details stay in the server logs.

### Development
- `MOCK_AI=1` runs without a key. Suggestions are deterministic fakes, and translations of the sample document are canned copies.
- Deployed on Vercel. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set as a production secret.

## Unreleased

### Added
- Translation cache. The server keeps up to 200 translations in instance memory, keyed by model, target language, and text. A repeat costs nothing and returns in milliseconds. Failed translations are never cached.
- Translating back to the previous language restores the original text in the browser, with no API call.

## 2026-10-30

### Added
- Interface language switch for pt-BR, en-US, es-AR, and zh-CN (`2de53c7`).
- "Text language" selector that translates the document with the co-author (`2de53c7`).
- Localized error messages through server error codes (`2de53c7`).
- Canned translations of the sample document in mock mode (`2de53c7`).
- AI session transcripts in `.claude/` and `.grok/` (`e3b5343`).

### Fixed

lines: # Mock "translations" are canned copies of the sample document (matched by its
# first heading), not translations of your text; other documents only get a marker.
+# Shared documents (Supabase Realtime + Postgres). Provisioned through the Vercel
+# Marketplace; `vercel env pull` fills these. Then run supabase/migrations/*.sql.
+# Leave empty to run single-user with collaboration off.
- Works on the selection, or on the whole document when nothing is selected. A selection gets the surrounding text and the document outline as context.
- Refine a suggestion with a follow-up instruction. The co-author keeps the earlier rounds as history. A failed refine keeps the previous suggestion.
- Six quick actions (Improve, Shorten, Expand, Fix grammar, More formal, More casual) plus a free-text instruction box (⌘K).
-- The document is saved in the browser. A pending suggestion is never saved.
+- A pending suggestion is never saved or shared.
+- Every document has its own URL (`/d/<id>`). Opening `/` creates a new document and redirects to it. Anyone with the link can edit.
+- Real-time co-editing with live cursors and a count of who is editing (Yjs over Supabase Realtime).

+- Documents are saved as an append-only log of edits in Postgres, so concurrent writers never overwrite each other. The table can't be read in bulk: a document loads only through a function that needs its id.
+- AI suggestions stay private to the person who asked. They are reviewed in an overlay, and only the accepted result is written to the shared document, as one edit.
+- If a collaborator changed the target text while the co-author was working or during the review, the suggestion is not applied and a message asks to try again.
+- The document language is shared: accepting a translation switches it for everyone.
+- Without Supabase settings the app still runs, single-user and unsaved, with a "collaboration off" note.
- Interface in English, Brazilian Portuguese, Argentine Spanish, and Simplified Chinese. Defaults to the browser language and is remembered.
- Server errors are codes, shown in the interface language. Upstream details stay in the server logs.
+- Collaboration needs a Supabase project (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and its public key) and the table in `supabase/migrations/0001_doc_updates.sql`.

+- Known limits: no compaction of the edit log yet; a whole-document translation is refused if anyone typed during its review; the last half-second of typing before a tab closes may be lost if the browser drops the final save.
- `MOCK_AI=1` runs without a key. Suggestions are deterministic fakes, and translations of the sample document are canned copies.
- Deployed on Vercel. `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set as a production secret.
+- Shared documents with a unique URL and real-time collaboration (see "Collaboration" above).

- Translation cache. The server keeps up to 200 translations in instance memory, keyed by model, target language, and text. A repeat costs nothing and returns in milliseconds. Failed translations are never cached.
- Translating back to the previous language restores the original text in the browser, with no API call.

content.text:
Shared documents are built and pass all single-tab tests, but the real-time and saving parts are untested. They need a Supabase database, and creating it requires you to accept the Supabase Marketplace terms in your browser. I didn't accept legal terms on your behalf.

**What you need to do:** open the link below, accept the terms, and tell me when it's done.

```
https://vercel.com/mondainis-projects/~/integrations/accept-terms/supabase?source=cli
```

After that I'll create the database in the same region as your functions, apply the table, run the two-tab tests and deploy.

**What's built**, on the `feat/shared-docs` branch:
- **Unique URLs.** Opening `/` creates a document at `/d/<id>`, with an unguessable id, and redirects to it. Your first document starts from the text saved in your browser, later ones from the sample.
- **Real-time editing.** Yjs synced over Supabase Realtime, with live cursors and a count of who's editing.
- **Saving.** Each edit is stored as its own row, so two people saving at once can't overwrite each other.
- **Private AI review.** Suggestions show only to the person who asked, in an overlay over the shared editor. Accepting writes the result to the shared document as one edit.
- **Conflict refusal.** If someone changed the target text meanwhile, the suggestion isn't applied and a message says so.
- **Shared document language.** Accepting a translation switches the language for everyone.
- **Fallback.** Without Supabase settings, the app runs single-user with a "collaboration off" note.

**Security fix from the side agent's warning:** it was right. My first table design let anyone with the public key read every document. The table now has no read access at all. A document loads only through a database function that needs its id.

**Tested so far.** Typecheck, lint and build pass. Two headless Chrome scripts ran against a mock-mode server: 13 checks for the main flows and 3 for refine. All pass, with no page errors. They covered:
- the redirect and seeding
- review staying private, then applied on accept
- reject leaving the document alone
- refine
- a translation setting the language, and translating back with no API call
- the conflict refusal when someone edits the target during a request

**Not tested yet:** syncing between two tabs, presence, saving and reloading, and production. All of these need the database.

The translation cache and changelog were committed directly on `main` before I created the branch. Everything since is uncommitted on the branch.

content.text:
Shared documents work locally against the real Supabase database, but they're not live. My production deploy was blocked by the permission classifier, so you'll need to run it.

```
! vercel deploy --prod
```

The Supabase settings are already in your production environment, so nothing else needs configuring. When the deploy finishes, I'll repeat the two-tab test against the live site.

**What I set up:**
- **Database:** Supabase was created through the Vercel Marketplace, in the same region as your functions, and connected to the project.
- **Table:** the edit log and its read function are applied.
- **Locked down:** the public role can only append edits. Probed from outside with the public key: a bulk read is refused, delete is refused, and a malformed id is rejected. Loading by id works. I also removed the update, delete and truncate rights that Supabase's defaults gave the public role, since row-level security doesn't block truncate.

**Two-tab test with the real database** (AI in mock mode), all 14 checks passed:
- The second tab opens the same document, and both show "2 people editing".
- Typing in one tab appears in the other, with a cursor label like "Guest 4962".
- An AI suggestion under review stays invisible to the other tab. Accepting it sends it to both, and the two texts end up identical.
- If the other person edits the target during the review, the accept is refused with the "text changed" message, and their edit survives.
- Accepting a translation switches the other tab's text language too.

Persistence was tested separately. I killed the whole browser, then opened the document in a brand-new browser profile with nobody else online. It loaded exactly the saved text, including the typed edits and the accepted AI change.

**Bug found and fixed:** someone joining later saw "Only you here" until the other person moved their cursor. Each tab now re-sends its presence when a newcomer arrives.

Nothing from this work is committed yet. It all sits uncommitted on the `feat/shared-docs` branch.
